prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hours; protection overrides regulation. Operations Control Centre’s Line Traffic Controller owns recovery/regulation, records incidents/first-safe-instruction, confirms Temporary Speed Restriction Notice/timetable visibility; station holds affect departure, not locking. Authority reviews incident/degradation/timetable consistency. Revenue Train Operator reports condition/hazards, repeats Voice Dispatch Console instructions; voice never replaces safety-data. Console displays calling-identity/platform/hold-reason; dispatch requires positive confirmation/cancellation distinct from timeout/failure/rejection. Field staff support fallback. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle; displays proposals before confirmation, separates commanded/locked/occupied states; coordinates timetable-deviation/closure/crowding before passenger release; station identifiers match controller workstations. Service Timetable Server supplies planned context; changes require approval. Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciled predictions/stopping-pattern/platform-updates; revised destination/skip-stop requires confirmed identity/route; closed-platform movements unavailable-for-boarding but operationally tracked. Local station staff receive validated-CBTC indications: normal/held/door-interlock-fault/radio-degraded/emergency-stop/evacuation-support. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance validates certificate-windows/clocks, supplies authentication and maintenance-window Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack/audit-reference; no safety changes. Train Radio Modem consumes pack before renewed station/passenger secure sessions. Cyber Security Officer approves renewed-security after review; reviews workstation rights at commissioning/material-change. Maintenance Diagnostic Server(Quarry) supplies nonvital diagnostics, records station faults/rejections/inconsistencies for Signal Maintenance Engineer(Maple), who records restoration clearance; no vital bypass. North District Zone Controller(Marble)/South District Zone Controller(Orchid) validate authorities/separation/locking. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking prove points/routes/releases; indications to zones/onboard; Axle Counter Reset Request/Route Release Exception List respectively. No reset with locked-routes/approaches; retain unexcluded hazards. Conflicting occupancy/lost correspondence restrictive; transfers require odometry/receiving-validation/reissue. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train-operation/fallback/cutout; authenticates/enforces authorities/speed/doors/profiles, cyclewise braking; reports rejection/degradation, Brake Curve Checksum Log, door-enable-side/berth/departure-readiness. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status

New part:
S150: During degraded operation, the CBTC system favours restrictive platform states and requires explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure support at the affected station.
S151: Diagnostics and maintenance for the Greenvale Metro communications-based train control system are organised around prompt event collection, controlled remote access, and traceable engineering decisions.
S152: Each safety-related part records time-stamped events for state changes, command acceptance, rejected commands, communication loss, and local protective actions.
S153: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives event streams from fixed and onboard equipment through monitored interfaces that do not allow maintenance traffic to alter train movement authority.
S154: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server uses the checksum log to compare stored braking data identifiers against the expected maintenance baseline for the affected train.
S155: Remote diagnostic sessions are initiated by a Signal Maintenance Engineer and are limited to read-only observation unless an approved maintenance window authorises a specific intervention.
S156: The Cyber Security Officer reviews privileged diagnostic access logs and confirms that remote connections use current credentials and approved encryption settings.
S157: The Line Traffic Controller receives the Route Release Exception List during incident triage and uses it to check whether a release anomaly could affect service recovery decisions.
S158: Marble records controller health, interface state, and fallback mode transitions in a form that can be correlated with adjacent wayside and operations records.
S159: The South District Zone Controller maintains comparable diagnostic coverage so that boundary events can be reviewed without relying on a single source of evidence.
S160: The East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report route command histories, point detection changes, and protective lock status to support failure localisation.
S161: The Atlas Onboard Controller stores onboard fault codes, movement authority acceptance records, propulsion cutback requests, and train interface exceptions for later retrieval.
S162: The Dual Channel Odometer provides distance and speed plausibility information that is retained with trainborne diagnostic records after any odometry disagreement.
S163: The Train Radio Modem records bearer loss, reconnection timing, signal quality indicators, and message retry counts needed to distinguish radio coverage issues from equipment faults.
S164: The Wayside Radio Access Network and Safety Data Communication Network provide communication performance records that are compared with controller logs during network-related investigations.
S165: The Metro Operations Control System displays selected fault summaries to the Line Traffic Controller but does not expose detailed maintenance commands at the traffic control workstation.
S166: A Revenue Train Operator reports observed cab indications, train handling effects, and passenger service impacts using the operational reporting channel defined for degraded service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
